title: Inputs and known answers
summary: A feature is an input used for a prediction. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Keep each input paired with the right answer.
introduction: A feature is an input used for a prediction. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Keep each input paired with the right answer. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A feature is an input used for a prediction. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Keep each input paired with the right answer.
The output is [2] 4. The second feature row has two pages, and its label has four fictional minutes.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Find the third input and its label.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Shuffling inputs without shuffling their matching labels breaks the pairs.
For more detail later, use this [Machine Learning further reading](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course).
